journey.label: Rheumatic fever at age five
journey.fortune_basis: It was really discouraging and kind of scary.
journey.quote: I became a physician because of an experience I had when I was five years old. I developed rheumatic fever, and at that time, there wasn't a lot that you could do.

journey.label: House-call pediatrician inspires medicine
journey.fortune_basis: I thought, that's what I want to do. I want to be like him.
journey.quote: We had a wonderful pediatrician who actually made house calls, and he was reassuring to my family and to me, and fortunately I did well.

journey.fortune_basis: it just it just fit. It just worked. It was a great place to practice.
journey.quote: So my faculty member made me aware of Kaiser Permanente, and I applied, and fortunately, that's where I began my career.

journey.quote: had made this mental note to myself before I even joined the group, I was not going to take on any leadership roles.

journey.year_note: "Early in my career as a physician"; no year given.

retellable.title: Coming back every month until told not to
retellable.summary: When Orange County's new centralized appointment call center collapsed at launch, Ken Bell asked Ellison to help fix it. He and administrator Priscilla Daniel visited every office monthly to listen until things improved over about a year and a half, and the model spread across KP.
retellable.quote: I will come back next month, and the month after that, and the month after that, and the month after that, until you tell me, I don't need to come here anymore.
retellable.why: A concrete lesson in change management and listening to the front lines.

retellable.title: The receptionist who saves lives
retellable.summary: A receptionist persuaded Mary Gonzalez, in for allergies, to book an overdue mammogram, which found an early cancer. Ellison uses it to show that every point of contact in an integrated system can close care gaps.
retellable.quote: She could say, my job is not just to check in patients, my job is to save lives.
retellable.why: Shows integrated care and prevention through one patient's experience.

retellable.title: Ken Bell tells him to stay
retellable.summary: Early in his career, as his father was dying back east, Ellison planned to return to work. His area medical director, Ken Bell, told him to stay, and he was with his father when he died while colleagues covered his patients.
retellable.quote: And he said, "no, you're not. You're staying right where you are. You're where you need to be, where you're supposed to be.
retellable.why: Illustrates collegial support he called the family of the medical group.

retellable.title: Turning surgical drapes into COVID masks
retellable.summary: Short of protective equipment early in COVID, SCPMG had a surplus of surgical drapes. Ellison and Greg Adams went to the Los Angeles garment district and found a sportswear maker to turn them into masks.
retellable.quote: Greg came to Southern Cal and he and I went down to the garment district in Los Angeles, and we found a sportswear manufacturer who was going to retool their equipment
retellable.why: A vivid example of improvised, real-time crisis leadership.
